newsitem.title: UK: LPC-Qatar $300 mln loan launched into syndication.
newsitem.headline: LPC-Qatar $300 mln loan launched into syndication.

text.p: LONDON Aug 6 (LPC) - The $300m five-year syndicated term loan for the State of Qatar has been launched into general syndication. The deal has a large arranging group, consisting of Bankgesellschaft Berlin, BoTM, Bayerische Landesbank, Commerzbank, DKB, GIB, Sakura, Saudi British Bank, SocGen and Sumitomo.

The deal, which is new money for Qatar, is priced at 32.5 bps over LIBOR for years one and two, rising to 35 bps for years three to five. Funds will be used to finance equity investment in petroleum projects, and repayment is in three equal semi- annual instalments starting on the fourth anniversary of signing, giving an average life of 4.5 years. The new loan is the State of Qatar's second transaction this year - SocGen led a $250 million term loan in January, which was priced at 42.5 bps, with a three-year grace period. The swift margin reduction combined with the longer grace period of the new deal has drawn criticism from the market, however the State of Qatar will only tap the syndicated loan market once more before its petroleum project revenues come on stream, which will eliminate the need to borrow abroad.

The syndication strategy has been contentious, as some banks in the lead group favoured top-tier segregation through the creation of a smaller arranging group, with a co-arranger group, which was the strategy favoured in the previous syndication. This deal will see the senior slot of co-arranger offered in general syndication, along with four other levels of participation.-- Tessa Walsh LPC Newsroom 44-0171-542-4048
